19.h: 15 - Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf al-Qurashī *
19.t:
Ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb ... ⟦1:171⟧
The Imam (الإمام), the hero, the lion, the Lion of Allah, Abū ʿUmārah, and Abū Yaʿlā, al-Qurashī, al-Hāshimī, al-Makkī, then al-Madanī, Badrī (البدري), the martyr.
The paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his brother through (1) fosterage.
Ibn Isḥāq said (2) : When Ḥamzah embraced Islam, Quraysh knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had become protected, and that Ḥamzah would protect him, so they refrained from some of what they used to inflict on him.
قال أبو إسحاق: عن حارثة بن مضرب، عن علي:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: (Call Ḥamzah) .
So I said: Who is the man with the red camel?
Ḥamzah said: He is ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah. So on that day Ḥamzah dueled ʿUtbah and killed him (3) .
وروى: أسامة بن زيد، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the women of the Anṣār weeping over their dead, and he said: (But Ḥamzah has no women to weep for him) .
So they came and wept over Ḥamzah in his presence, until he said: (Order them not to weep for any deceased after ⟦1:172⟧ today (1)) .
And in the book al-Mustadrak by al-Ḥākim:
From Jābir, raised (المرفوع): (The chief of the martyrs: Ḥamzah, and a man who stood up to an unjust ruler, commanded him and forbade him, and he killed him) (2) .
I say: its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is weak (ضعيف).
الدغولي (3) : حدثنا أحمد بن سيار، حدثنا رافع بن أشرس، حدثنا خليد الصفار، عن إبراهيم الصائغ، عن عطاء، عن جابر:
From the Prophet ﷺ, he said: (The chief of the martyrs is Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib (4)) .
This is gharīb (الغريب). ⟦1:173⟧
أسامة بن زيد: عن نافع، عن ابن عمر، قال:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned on the day of Uḥud and heard the women of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal weeping over their dead.
He said: (But Ḥamzah has no women to weep for him) .
So the women of the Anṣār came and wept over Ḥamzah in his presence; he fell asleep, then woke while they were still weeping.
He said: (Woe to them! Are they still here until now? Order them to go back, and not to weep for any deceased after today (1)) .
ابن إسحاق: حدثني عبد الله بن الفضل بن العباس بن ربيعة، عن سليمان بن يسار، عن جعفر بن عمرو بن أمية الضمري، قال:
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār and I went out on a raid in the time of Muʿāwiyah, and we passed by Ḥimṣ, and Waḥshī was there.
Ibn ʿAdī said: Would you like us to ask Waḥshī how he killed Ḥamzah?
So we went out looking for him and asked about him, and we were told: You will find him in the courtyard of his house, on a rug of his; he is a man overcome by wine, but if you find him sober, you will find an Arab man.
We came to him, and there we found a very old black man, like a bughāth bird (2) , on a rug of his, and he was sober, so we greeted him.
He raised his head to ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAdī and said: A son of ʿAdī? By Allah, you are the son of al-Khiyār.
He said: Yes.
He said: By Allah, I have not seen you since I handed you to your mother, the woman of Banū Saʿd who nursed you at Dhū Ṭuwā, while she was on her camel, and your feet gleamed before me.
We said: We have come for you to tell us how you killed Ḥamzah.
He said: I shall tell you what I told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:
I was the slave of Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, and his uncle Ṭuʿaymah ibn ʿAdī had been killed on the day of Badr.
He said to me: If you kill Ḥamzah ⟦1:174⟧ you are free.
I was a man with a spear that I would throw, and I seldom missed with it. I went out with the people, and when they met I took my spear and went out watching for Ḥamzah, until I saw him in the midst of the people like an ashen camel (1) , crushing people with his sword, sparing (2) nothing. By Allah, I was making ready for him when Sibāʿ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā al-Khuzāʿī went ahead of me to him.
When Ḥamzah saw him, he said: Come to me, O son of the woman who cuts clitorises (3) .
Then Ḥamzah struck him, and by Allah it was as though (4) he did not miss his head; I never saw anything faster than the fall of his head.
I balanced my spear until I was satisfied with it, then hurled it at him, and it struck him in his lower belly (5) , until it came out between his legs. He fell, and tried to rise (6) , but was overcome, so I left him with it until he died. Then I went to him, took my spear, and returned to the camp and sat in it, for I had no need of anything else.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Mecca, I fled to al-Ṭāʾif. When the delegation of al-Ṭāʾif went out to embrace Islam, the earth, vast as it is, became narrow for me, and I said: I will go to Syria, or Yemen, or some other land. By Allah, I was in that worry of mine when a man said:
By Allah, Muḥammad does not (7) kill anyone who enters his religion. So I went out until ⟦1:175⟧ I came to Medina, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: (Waḥshī?) .
I said: Yes.
He said: (Sit down, and tell me how you killed Ḥamzah) .
So I told him as I am telling you.
He said: (Woe to you! Hide your face from me, and let me not see you) .
So I used to keep away (1) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wherever he was, until he passed away.
When the Muslims went out against Musaylimah, I went out with them with my spear with which I had killed Ḥamzah. When the people met, I looked at Musaylimah with the sword in his hand, and by Allah I did not know him, and there was a man of the Anṣār wanting him from the other side, and each of us was making ready for him.
When I had the chance, I hurled my spear at him and it struck him, and the Anṣārī charged at him and struck him with the sword, and your Lord knows best which of us killed him.
If I killed him, then I have killed the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I have killed the worst of people (2) .
وبه: عن سليمان بن يسار، عن عبد الله بن عمر، قال:
I heard a man saying: The black slave killed him, -meaning: Musaylimah-. ⟦1:176⟧
أسامة بن زيد: عن الزهري، عن أنس، قال:
On the day of Uḥud, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood over Ḥamzah, whose nose had been cut off and who had been mutilated.
He said: (Were it not that Ṣafiyyah would grieve within herself, I would leave him until Allah gathers him from the bellies of the beasts and the birds) .
He was shrouded in a striped woollen cloak; when his head was covered his feet showed, and when his feet were covered his head showed. And he did not pray over any of the martyrs.
And he said: (I am a witness over you) .
He would put three in one grave, and two, and would ask: Which of them knew more of the Qurʾān? and would put him first in the niche of the grave.
And he shrouded two men and three in one garment (1) .
ابن عون: عن عمير بن إسحاق، عن سعد بن أبي وقاص، قال:
Ḥamzah was fighting on the day of Uḥud in front of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with two swords, saying: I am the Lion of Allah (2) .
رواه: يونس بن بكير، عن ابن عون، عن عمير, as mursal (مرسل), and he added:
He stumbled (3) and fell on his back, and the mail coat slipped off his belly, so the Abyssinian slave speared him (4) and ripped his belly open (5) .
عبد العزيز بن الماجشون: عن عبد الله بن الفضل، عن سليمان بن يسار، ⟦1:177⟧ عن جعفر بن عمرو الضمري، قال:
I went out with Ibn al-Khiyār to Syria, and we asked about Waḥshī, and it was said: There he is in the shade of his palace, as though he were a bloated skin-bag (1) .
We came and greeted him, and stood (2) a little while. Ibn al-Khiyār had his turban wrapped about his head, so that Waḥshī could see only his eyes and his feet.
He said: O Waḥshī! Do you know me?
He said: No, by Allah, except that I know that ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār married a woman called Umm Qitāl bint Abī al-ʿĪṣ, and she bore a boy in Mecca, and I sought a wet nurse for him, and I carried him with his mother and handed him to her; it is as though I am looking at your feet.
He said: So ʿUbayd Allāh uncovered his face, then said: Will you not tell us about the killing of Ḥamzah?
He said: Yes. He killed Ṭuʿaymah ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Khiyār at Badr, so my master Jubayr said to me:
If you kill Ḥamzah in revenge for my uncle, you are free.
When the people went out from (3) ʿAynayn - and ʿAynūn is a mountain below Uḥud, with a valley between it and Uḥud - Sibāʿ said: Is there anyone to duel?
Ḥamzah said: O son of the woman who cuts clitorises! Do you oppose Allah and His Messenger?
Then he charged at him, and he became like yesterday gone by.
I lay in wait for Ḥamzah beneath a rock until he passed by me (4) , and I hit him with my spear in his lower belly, until the spear came out of his hip.
Until he said: I was in al-Ṭāʾif, and they sent messengers to the Prophet ﷺ, and it was said: He does not harm (5) messengers.
So I went out with them, and when he saw me, he said: (Are you Waḥshī?) .
I said: Yes.
He said: (The one who killed Ḥamzah?) .
I said: Yes, the matter was as has reached you.
He said: (Can you not ⟦1:178⟧ hide your face from me?) .
He said: So I went back.
When he passed away and Musaylimah rose up, I said: I shall surely go out against him; perhaps I will kill him and so make amends for Ḥamzah through him.
So I went out with the people, and their affair was what it was, and there was a man standing in a gap in a wall, as though he were an ashen (1) camel, his hair dishevelled. I threw my spear at him and put it between his breasts until it came out from between his shoulders, and a man of the Anṣār leapt at him and struck him with the sword on the crown of his head.
Sulaymān ibn Yasār said: Then I heard Ibn ʿUmar saying:
A slave girl said on the roof of a house: The Commander of the Faithful (أمير المؤمنين), the black slave has killed him (2) .
Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah said: Then the Muslims spread out seeking their slain, and they found no slain man but that they had mutilated him, except Ḥanẓalah ibn Abī ʿĀmir; his father Abū ʿĀmir was with the polytheists, so he was left for his sake.
They claim that his father stood over him as he lay slain and pushed his chest with his foot.
Then he said: Two debts you have incurred; I warned you beforehand about this death of yours, O Dunays. By the life of Allah, you used to uphold ties of kinship and be dutiful to your father.
They found Ḥamzah with his belly ripped open, and Waḥshī had carried his liver to Hind, in fulfilment of a vow she had made when he killed her father on the day of Badr. He was buried in a striped cloak he had on; when it was drawn up to his head his feet showed, so they covered his feet with some plants.
ابن إسحاق: حدثني بريدة، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي:
The Messenger of Allah (3) ﷺ said: (If I gain victory over Quraysh, I shall mutilate thirty of them) .
When the companions of the Messenger ⟦1:179⟧ of Allah ﷺ saw his grief, they said:
If we gain victory over them, we shall mutilate them as no one among the Arabs has ever mutilated anyone.
Then Allah revealed: “And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished” (Qurʾān 16:126) to the end of the sūrah.
So the Messenger of Allah (1) ﷺ pardoned.
أبو بكر بن عياش: عن يزيد بن أبي زياد، عن مقسم، عن ابن عباس، قال:
When Ḥamzah was killed, his sister Ṣafiyyah came forward and met ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, and they made her think that they did not know.
She came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: (I fear for her mind) .
He placed his hand on her chest and prayed for her, and she said: To Allah we belong and to Him we return, and wept.
Then he came and stood over him, and he had been mutilated, and he said: (Were it not for the grief of the women, I would leave him until he is gathered from the crops of the birds and the bellies of the beasts) .
Then he gave orders concerning the slain, and he began praying over them with seven takbīrs, and they would be lifted away while Ḥamzah was left; then seven more would be brought and he would say the takbīr seven times over them, until he finished with them (2) . ⟦1:180⟧
Yazīd is not an authority (الحجة), and the statement of Jābir, “He did not pray over them,” is more authentic (الصحيح) (1) .
And in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (الصحيحين), from the hadith of ʿUqbah:
That the Prophet ﷺ prayed over the slain of Uḥud as he prays over the dead.
This was some days before his death (2) . ⟦1:181⟧
It is narrated from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayrah, his saying -peace be upon him-: (If I gain victory over Quraysh, I shall mutilate seventy of them) .
Then was revealed: “And if you punish ...” , the verse (1) .
عبدان: أخبرنا عيسى بن عبيد الكندي، حدثني ربيع بن أنس، حدثني أبو العالية، عن أبي بن كعب:
That seventy of the Anṣār were struck down on the day of Uḥud. He said: And they mutilated their slain.
The Anṣār said: If we ever strike them on some day, we shall surely exceed them.
When it was the day of the conquest of Mecca, a man who was not known called out: No Quraysh after today! twice.
Then Allah revealed to His Prophet: “And if you punish ...” , the verse.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Refrain from the people) (2) . ⟦1:182⟧
يونس بن بكير: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، قال:
Ṣafiyyah came on the day of Uḥud with two garments for Ḥamzah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw her, he disliked that she should see Ḥamzah in his condition, so he sent al-Zubayr to her to hold her back, and he took the two garments.
Beside Ḥamzah was a slain man of the Anṣār, and they disliked choosing for Ḥamzah.
He said: (Cast lots between them, and whichever of them gets the better of the two garments, it is his) .
So they cast lots between them, and Ḥamzah was shrouded in one garment and the Anṣārī in one garment (1) .
ابن إسحاق: عن إسماعيل بن أمية، عن أبي الزبير، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قال:
The Prophet ﷺ said: (When your brothers were struck down at Uḥud, Allah placed their souls inside green birds that come down to the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and shelter in lamps of gold hanging in the shade of the Throne.
When they found the goodness of their food, their drink and their resting place, they said:
Who will convey to our brothers from us that we are alive in Paradise, being provided for, so that they do not shrink back in war and do not lose their desire for jihad?
Allah said: I will convey it to them from you) . ⟦1:183⟧
Then was revealed: “And do not think of those who are killed in the way of Allah as dead” (Qurʾān 3 (1) :169) .
ابن إسحاق: حدثني عاصم بن عمر، عن عبد الرحمن بن جابر بن عبد الله، عن أبيه:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, when he mentioned the people of Uḥud: (By Allah, I wish I had been left with the companions of the mountain's foot (2)) .
He means: killed along with them.
And it has come with a chain of transmission (الإسناد) in which there is weakness, from Jābir:
That when the Prophet ﷺ saw Ḥamzah slain he wept, and when he saw how he had been mutilated he gasped (3) . ⟦1:184⟧
